lines.text: In this town, touch the statue's nose after noon and the Pigeon Mayor takes your hat.
You see, he's a very fast pigeon.
Mr. Pickett touched it once.
Now he walks around with a bare head and a sunburn.
The barber only cuts hair before noon.
He does it out of pure panic.
Mrs. Lund wears seven hats so she can afford to lose six.
The mayor's hat is bolted on with a very large bolt.
I'm Pearl, and I've never owned a hat.
My head's too round for any of them.
I only have a paper birthday crown in my pocket.
Nobody's ever tried to steal it. Nobody wants it.
My little brother Milo just learned to reach.
He loves noses.
Until one noon, Milo spotted the statue.
He pointed. He giggled.
Mom was buying pickles. Nobody was watching.
The clock struck noon.
First, his fingers grabbed the fence.
Then he crawled onto the fountain edge.
Pigeons turned their heads. All of them.
Then his hand stopped an inch from the nose.
Mrs. Lund gasped and clutched all seven hats.
I froze. Then I remembered the rule.
Touch the nose, lose your hat.
Not your shirt. Not your shoes.
Just hats.
And I'd never owned one.
The rule never said anything about crowns.
I plopped my paper crown on Milo's head.
He booped the nose.
Boop.
Pigeons exploded off the rooftops.
The Pigeon Mayor landed on Milo.
He glared at the crown.
A paper crown. Nobody had tried that.
He snatched it and flew off.
Milo laughed. The pigeons did not.
The Pigeon Mayor wears it to every meeting.
It looks better on him.
In this town, nobody touches the nose after noon, except me.

post.title: Never touch the nose after noon or the Pigeon Mayor comes
post.description: Pearl has no hat, but her baby brother loves noses. One paper crown might save the day.

card.price: Mr. Pickett touched it once. Now he walks around with a bare head and a sunburn.
card.title: The Hat Tax
card.twist: At noon the brother's fingers get closer: first the fence, then the fountain edge, then an inch from the nose. Pearl swaps him her paper crown, which isn't a hat, so the Pigeon Mayor takes it and leaves them both alone. The rule only takes hats, and she never owned one.
card.closer: In this town, nobody touches the nose after noon, except Pearl, who just lost a paper crown.
card.opener: In this town, if you touch the fountain statue's nose after noon, the Pigeon Mayor takes your hat forever.
card.teaser: Her brother reached for the nose. She had one paper thing.
card.premise: Everyone in the square keeps their hands off the statue's nose, but Pearl, the one kid with no hat, has a little brother who just learned to reach and loves noses.
examples: The barber only cuts hair before noon, out of pure panic.
Mrs. Lund wears seven hats so she can afford to lose six.
The mayor's hat is bolted to his head with a very large bolt.
